title: 高三多题听力：步道与演出
instruction: 听四段较长对话和一段独白，五组分别回答2、3、3、4、3题，共15题，每题三选。每段听两遍；听前每题5秒读题，听后每题5秒作答，已含在音轨中。来源题面/印本附注脚本/参考键可核，原音轨未取得；本稿提供完整原创音频与脚本。
source_form_notice: 高三公开阶段卷第二节五材料2/3/3/4/3、三选、两遍结构已核；附印本注释脚本及参考键，原录音缺、原校及地域学期未认证，不当gold。本稿完整原创配套供审阅。
teacher_source_notice: 公开标签为雅礼相关阶段卷，正文只确认高三英语，地域与学期未在正文确认，学校原版未认证。原题面、附注印本脚本与参考键在库；脚本为带题号/词汇注释的OCR文本，未认证清洁逐字/独立听校，原音轨未取得，源全输入未通过，不当gold。
source_scoring_notice: 来源本节15题、每题1.5分、满分22.5分为明确印出配置，非年级统一标准。

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: The new footpath looks shorter on the map. Shall we take it to the station?

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: It is shorter, but the last section has no lighting. By the time we leave the concert it will be dark.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Then we should use the main road tonight, even if it takes ten minutes longer.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: Agreed. We can try the footpath on our way to the market on Saturday morning.

questions.stem: Why will the speakers avoid the footpath tonight?
options: It is closed for building work.
It is much longer than the main road.
Part of it will be unlit.
questions.rationale: 末段无灯且回程天黑；A无封路，B更短。

questions.stem: When might they try the footpath?
questions.rationale: 末句周六早去市场时尝试；B/C与决定冲突。

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: The audience survey says the afternoon performance was too quiet. Should we turn up the speakers for the evening?

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Look at where those people were sitting. Most were behind the pillar, while people near the front said the sound was clear.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: So a louder setting might make the front rows uncomfortable.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Exactly. Let us test the speaker position first. Move one slightly sideways, and ask someone to listen from each section.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: We have half an hour before the doors open.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Then test one change, make notes and leave enough time to restore the old position if it is worse. We should not keep experimenting after the audience arrives.

questions.stem: What pattern does the woman notice?
options: Complaints came mainly from behind a pillar.
All seating areas reported the same problem.
questions.rationale: 多数抱怨者在柱后，前排清楚；A/C不符。

questions.stem: Why might increasing the volume be unsuitable?
options: It could make sound uncomfortable near the front.
The speakers have no volume controls.
The evening show has been cancelled.
questions.rationale: M据前排已清楚推音量更大会不适；B/C无。

questions.stem: What does the woman suggest doing?
options: Waiting until the audience is seated.
questions.rationale: 先测一个位置并留恢复时间；A/B相反。

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: The map for our cycling group marks a café beside the canal. Can we stop there for lunch?

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: It seats only eight people indoors, and there will be fourteen of us. I called to ask whether they could serve us in two groups.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: What did they say?

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: They can prepare packed lunches if we order by Thursday. We could collect them and eat at the covered picnic area a little farther along.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: That sounds better than leaving half the group outside waiting. What about people who want to bring their own food?

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: That is fine. I will ask everyone to choose on the booking form, so we order only what is needed.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: And tell them the picnic area has no drinking-water tap. They should fill their bottles before we set off.

questions.stem: Why is an indoor café lunch unsuitable for the whole group?
options: The café opens only in the evening.
There are fewer indoor seats than cyclists.
The café does not serve any food.

questions.stem: What arrangement does the man propose?
options: Collect ordered lunches and eat farther along.
Cancel the trip unless everyone buys lunch.
Leave half the cyclists at the starting point.
questions.rationale: 可预订午餐去有顶野餐点；B可自带，C非方案。

questions.stem: What should cyclists do before setting off?
options: Return the booking forms to the café.
questions.rationale: 野餐点无饮水龙头，需出发前灌水；A/B无要求。

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: The actor playing the uncle is ill. I suppose we must cancel Friday's performance.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Not necessarily. Lena knows the part from rehearsals, but she has never performed it in front of an audience.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: Could she read from a script? It might look unfinished.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: We can explain the change honestly at the start. I would rather let her hold the script than make her spend two days memorising every line under pressure.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: The other actors will need to adjust their movements too.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Yes. We will rehearse the scenes with her this afternoon, especially the doorway scene where timing matters.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: Should we shorten that scene?

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Only if the movement cannot be made safe and clear. Do not cut the character's explanation merely to hide the replacement.

turns.speaker: M
turns.text: I will contact the group and ask them to arrive early.

turns.speaker: W
turns.text: Please also tell the ticket desk. People should hear about the change before they decide whether to attend.

questions.stem: Why is the original plan being reconsidered?
What is the woman's view of Lena using a script?
options: It must be hidden from the audience.
It is acceptable with an honest explanation.
It proves the performance must be cancelled.
questions.rationale: 支持公开说明、可持稿减压；A/C相反。

questions.stem: What will rehearsals focus on particularly?
options: A scene with important movement timing.

questions.stem: Why should the ticket desk be informed?
options: So people know the change before deciding to attend.
So the replacement actor can sell every ticket.
So all seats can be made free immediately.

turns.speaker: N
turns.text:
The recordings in this room come from a project on local accents. Volunteers read a short standard passage and then described a childhood memory in their own words. We used both tasks because reading the same words allows comparison, while an unscripted memory may reveal features that disappear in careful reading.

These recordings do not represent every voice in the district. Most volunteers heard about the project through one community centre, so people who rarely visit that centre may be missing. The map shows where speakers said they grew up, not where a particular accent begins or ends. Neighbours can speak differently, and people may change their speech in different situations.

Please use the headphones rather than playing the clips through your phone. The speakers agreed to use in this exhibition; that agreement does not automatically permit visitors to upload copies elsewhere. If you would like to study a recording further, speak to the project team about the appropriate access arrangements. We can discuss requests without assuming that public listening is the same as unrestricted reuse.

questions.stem: Why were two speaking tasks used?
options: To test which volunteers read fastest.
To compare common words and hear less scripted speech.
To make every person tell the same memory.
questions.rationale: 同读便比较，自述显自然特征；A速度非目标，C记忆各自。

questions.stem: What limitation of the collection is acknowledged?
options: Some parts of the community may be underrepresented.
No volunteers grew up in the district.
Every speaker used exactly the same accent.
questions.rationale: 一中心招募可能漏常不到者；B/C未支持。

questions.stem: What should visitors do before seeking further use of a recording?
options: Upload a copy to prove their interest.
Treat exhibition access as unrestricted permission.
Discuss access with the project team.
questions.rationale: 授权展览不等任意上传，进一步使用先找团队；A/B相反。
